schema.build: raw (the whole file as a bytes spec), or: payload (a name in `payloads`: the payload's exact text), members (a name in `sets` or a list, in file order; member 0 included), prefix (bytes before the first header), end (two, one or none zero blocks; two when absent), after (bytes after the end), zeroFrom (every byte from this offset on is set to zero) and then cut (only the first n bytes are kept). A member: name, data (a name in `data` or a bytes spec) or envelope, header (fields written over the writer's own, each a bytes spec placed at the field's start, the rest of the field NUL; a checksum given here is written as is, otherwise it is computed last over the header as written), size (the header's size value when it differs from the data), pad (the bytes after the data in place of the zero padding)
schema.envelope: member 0's data. Its text is exactly {"payloadType":<JSON string>,"payload":"<standard base64 with padding of the payload's UTF-8 bytes>","signatures":[<entries joined by a comma>]} with no whitespace; an entry is {"keyid":"<64 hex>","sig":"<88 base64 characters>"}. Fields: payload (another name in `payloads`), payloadType (the release type when absent), sign (test: the embedded test key, the default; other: a second key the key set does not hold; none: no entry), keyid (signer: the signing key's id, the default; test: the embedded key's id; absent: the entry is {"sig":…}), tamperSig (the first signature byte has its lowest bit flipped), junkSignatures (n entries {"keyid":"","sig":"<86 A, then ==>"} before the signed one), padTo (a last key "pad" whose value of the letter a brings the envelope to exactly n bytes: ,"pad":"aaa…" before the closing brace), raw (the data given as a bytes spec, no envelope at all). The signature is Ed25519 over DSSEv1 PAE (record §2.3); a key's id is the lower-case hex sha256 of its SPKI DER
schema.bytes: a string (latin1 text); {text} (UTF-8); {hex}; {fill: <one byte in hex>, length}; {counter: {length, mul, add}} (byte i = (i × mul + add) mod 256); {seq: {count, pad, before, after}} (for i from 0 to count − 1: before, i in decimal zero-padded to pad digits, after; all joined, UTF-8); {parts: [...]}. A payload in `payloads` is its exact text as a string, or a bytes spec
schema.expect: import: answer (§3.5: refused, staged, confirm, closed); code and params (§2.10, §3.5 "The types"); notices; dialog (true: the file dialog opened and gave the file; false: refused before it; closed: it opened and was closed); log (null: no line; else the event, its fields in order, and `line`, the exact update.log line for the host's os and now, absent where a field is the thrown error's own, shown as <thrown>); after (the drive: staged = the version validly staged or null; stagedTxt and stagedJson = those files' exact bytes; names = the only names in updates/staging/<v>/; absent, present; unchanged = the same tree, byte for byte, as before, and a path that was absent before is still absent: updates/staging/ and the folders under it are made by the data pass, never earlier (record 4.5, T6.0 fix 5); nothingWritten). log.unstated: the record does not say whether a line is written, and the runner asserts nothing about it. calls: answers, one per channel call of `calls` in order (a step that is no channel call has none; a run's answer stands at its own call's place), lines = every import line appended, in order. start: status (the fields of updates:status's drive part that matter), lines (the staging-swept lines, in order), removed, unchanged. discard: answer, lines, after. A line stands where the log can be written (§5.3 "Where"): a prepared drive whose updates/ is a real folder
